what_it_does: Large language models running on phones and embedded devices are bottlenecked by one expensive operation: multiplying a big matrix of stored model weights by a vector of current values (called a general matrix-vector multiply, or GEMV). This paper proposes PIMPAL, a design that moves that multiplication work inside the memory chips themselves rather than shipping data to a separate processor. Instead of doing the math the traditional way, PIMPAL precomputes lookup tables — small reference tables that store partial answers — and the memory hardware consults those tables in parallel across many memory sub-banks simultaneously. Two additional tricks are included: a smarter way to arrange data so the lookup tables are reused without extra memory reads (called locality-aware compute mapping), and a method to combine results from several small tables to support different numeric precisions. Based on the abstract, this appears promising for low-power edge devices, though the exact area and energy numbers would need to be verified in the full paper.
